label: FIXTURE RESULT: Stage 5 evaluation (recorded window, frozen bundle)

attempts.validity: all complete True, pending max 5.0, failures 0, server errors 0.0, pool timeouts 0, other edges 0

A.rule: no failed deliveries and pending stayed low

report.summary: No delay observed in this window. The outbox kept pace with arrivals, oldest undelivered age stayed near 1 s, and consumer delivery took about 71 ms. Late notifications are not reproduced here.

findings.claim: The outbox is not backing up: arrivals and publications match and pending stays at 2-5.
findings.reason: 541 arrivals vs 540 publications over 150 s, 0 failed, pending 2-5, oldest undelivered age max 1.18 s.

findings.claim: Delivery attempts are fast and all succeed on the first attempt, with no retries or errors.
findings.reason: 540 of 540 attempts succeeded; p95 total was 73.6 ms, almost all of it consumer auth time.

findings.claim: Transfer requests, the DB pool and DB blocking show no contention in the window.
findings.reason: No 5xx, p99 0.248 s, 0 pool timeouts, 0 pending borrowers, 0 blocked sessions.

limitations: Pending and pool gauges are sampled every 5 s and blocking every 2 s, so brief spikes could be missed.
E3 lists only the earliest 100 of 540 records, though the outcome counts cover all of them.
next_checks: Re-run the diagnosis over a window matching customer reports of late notifications, ideally under higher load.
Check the downstream notification channel (push/SMS provider) latency beyond the outbox consumer.

alternatives.reason: Only this window was inspected, and its load was steady at about 3.6/s.
alternatives.hypothesis: Lateness occurred outside this 150 s window, for example during a burst or consumer slowdown.

alternatives.reason: Timings only cover the call to the fixture consumer, not customer-facing delivery.
alternatives.hypothesis: Delay occurs downstream of LedgerCore's recorded publication, such as in push or SMS delivery to customers.

report.summary: In the window, outbox deliveries kept pace with arrivals with ~1s max age, no failures, and fast consumer responses. Late notifications are not reproduced in this window.

findings.claim: Outbox publications kept up with committed arrivals (540 vs 541, backlog of 1) and the pending count stayed at 2-5.
findings.reason: Arrivals and publications were both about 3.6/s; pending stayed flat and the outbox was settled.

findings.claim: The oldest undelivered event was never older than about 1.2 s, consistent with the 1 s poll interval.
findings.reason: Max oldest_undelivered_age was 1.18 s; outboxPollIntervalMs is 1000.

findings.claim: All 540 delivery attempts succeeded on attempt 1 with ~71 ms latency, almost all of it consumer auth time; no retries, errors or timeouts.
findings.reason: Outcomes were 540 success and 0 failures; the p95 was 73.6 ms against a 3 s delivery timeout.

limitations: The window is only 150 s; the lateness customers report may have occurred at another time.
Gauges are sampled every 2-5 s and delivery logs list only the first 100 of 540 records, so brief spikes could be missed.
next_checks: Re-run the diagnostics over the window when customers saw delays, using specific late transfer IDs.
Check the downstream notification provider's latency and queueing after the consumer endpoint.

alternatives.reason: No pool waiters or timeouts, and no blocked sessions in 75 samples.
alternatives.hypothesis: DB pool exhaustion or lock blocking delayed publishing

alternatives.reason: Only the fixture consumer's response time was measured, not end-user delivery.
alternatives.hypothesis: Delay occurs downstream of the consumer (e.g., push/SMS provider) or outside this window
